posts.title: A cleaner path to rare earth metals
posts.summary: Tomás Villalón Jr. ’14 was raised in San Antonio, Texas, but vividly remembers smog hanging over the city his family came from—Monterrey, Mexico, a steel manufacturing and metal fabrication hub. Even as a child, he realized it was problematic to breathe that air.  “I’m motivated because I’ve seen what metal-making does,” says Villalón, who majored…
bullets: Phoenix Tailings, an MIT-founded startup, has developed a proprietary electrochemical process to extract rare earth metals directly from existing mining waste.
The technology addresses the massive environmental footprint of the mining industry, which currently generates billions of tons of waste annually.
The company claims its extraction method is entirely toxin-free and can operate with zero carbon emissions when powered by renewable energy sources.

This innovation represents a significant shift in sustainable metallurgy, potentially securing critical mineral supply chains while mitigating the environmental impact of traditional metal production.

posts.title: Robotic therapy for stroke patients
posts.summary: Strokes leave 5 million people with long-term impairments each year, and a growing shortage of physical therapists makes it hard for them to get the care they need. A new approach tries to solve that problem by combining artificial intelligence and human therapy.  Johannes Lachner, a former MIT postdoc who is now an assistant professor…
bullets: A new robotic rehabilitation system utilizes generative AI and real-time force feedback to provide personalized physical therapy support for stroke survivors.
The technology is designed to learn from human physical therapists, allowing the system to offer precise assistance during daily living tasks and motor exercises.

The project aims to address the global shortage of physical therapists by extending their reach rather than replacing them, with upcoming clinical studies planned to evaluate therapist-specific models.
Beyond healthcare, the developers envision potential applications for this adaptive robotic technology in industrial settings and collaborative workspaces.

posts.title: Melt it, spin it, use it again
posts.summary: The average American throws out around 81 pounds of clothing each year, and there are few options for recycling it. MIT engineers hope to cut down on that textile waste with a new type of yarn.  The thermoplastic yarn mimics the properties of conventional elastic yarns, which typically combine spandex with polyester or nylon. Those…
bullets: MIT engineers have developed a new thermoplastic yarn made from polyethylene that mimics the strength and elasticity of traditional spandex-based textiles.
Unlike conventional elastic yarns that combine incompatible materials like spandex and polyester, this new material allows for full recyclability because it is composed of a single chemical family.

The yarn maintains its structural integrity and flexibility even after being melted and respun 10 times, offering a potential solution to the 81 pounds of textile waste generated per American annually.
The researchers are currently moving toward the weaving and knitting phase, aiming to create a circular economy for garments that can be easily processed in standard recycling facilities.

posts.title: Li Auto launches Lianshan in-house EV tech system, backs self-developed batteries with lifetime safety pledges
posts.summary:
The launch comes as Li Auto shifts its batteries from CATL to in-house developed ones produced by its joint venture with Sunwoda.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Li Auto has launched the 'Lianshan' system, an integrated in-house powertrain platform covering battery technology, electric drive units, and charging infrastructure.
The company is transitioning away from CATL batteries to in-house units produced through a 50-50 joint venture with Sunwoda, in which Li Auto is also taking an 8.79% direct equity stake.

To mitigate consumer concerns regarding the shift from premium CATL batteries, Li Auto is offering lifetime guarantees against battery self-ignition and post-collision fires, including full vehicle replacement if specific criteria are met.
This strategic pivot represents a significant vertical integration effort, allowing Li Auto to control its entire electric power ecosystem while reducing reliance on external battery suppliers.

posts.title: Muse Spark Open, Meta + Apple, Thin and Thick
posts.summary: Meta has a new open source model, and to everyone's surprise, they are are partnering with Apple to make sure you can run it locally.
bullets: Meta has released a new open-source AI model, signaling a continued commitment to an open ecosystem strategy.
In a surprising strategic shift, Meta is partnering with Apple to enable the local execution of this model on Apple hardware.
This collaboration highlights the growing importance of on-device AI performance and the evolving relationship between major platform holders and AI developers.
